statements.label: supported
statements.text: Screening for targeted monogenic conditions in addition to chromosomal aberrations increased the detection rate by 60.7%.
statements.evidence: The inclusion of targeted monogenic conditions alongside chromosomal aberrations led to a 60.7% increase (from 61 to 98) in the detection rate.
statements.note: The abstract reports a 60.7% rise in detections (from 61 to 98) when monogenic conditions were added to chromosomal screening.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The comprehensive cfDNA screening test reached similar sensitivity in pregnancies at average risk for fetal genetic conditions.
statements.evidence: pregnant women at elevated risk for fetal genetic conditions were enrolled for a cfDNA screening test based on coordinative allele-aware target enrichment sequencing.
statements.note: Only women at elevated risk were enrolled, so the abstract gives no performance figures for average-risk pregnancies.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with invasive prenatal or postnatal diagnostics, the screen found a genetic alteration in 135 pregnancies, with 98.5% sensitivity and 99.3% specificity.
statements.evidence: The comprehensive cfDNA screening detected a genetic alteration in 135 pregnancies with 98.5% sensitivity and 99.3% specificity relative to standard diagnostics.
statements.note: The abstract states 135 detected alterations with 98.5% sensitivity and 99.3% specificity against standard diagnostic testing.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among fetuses with ultrasound-suspected structural anomalies, aneuploidies made up 56.1% of the alterations the cfDNA screen identified, and single-gene variants 37.8%.
statements.evidence: Of 876 fetuses with suspected structural anomalies on ultrasound examination, comprehensive cfDNA screening identified 55 (56.1%) aneuploidies, 6 (6.1%) microdeletions and 37 (37.8%) single-gene pathogenic variants.
statements.note: In the 876 fetuses with structural anomalies the screen found 55 aneuploidies (56.1%), 6 microdeletions (6.1%) and 37 single-gene variants (37.8%).

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the 124-patient training set, cfDNA methylation markers separated PDAC from both healthy controls and colorectal cancer controls.
statements.evidence: In the training set (n=124 patients), cfDNA methylation markers distinguished PDAC from healthy and CRC controls.
statements.note: The training-set result states that the methylation markers distinguished PDAC from healthy and CRC controls.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the testing set, adding LRG1 to CA19-9 raised the AUC for early-stage PDAC from 0.88 to 0.92, with p=0.02.
statements.evidence: testing set of 86 early stage PDAC and 86 matched healthy controls, CA19-9 had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.88 (95% CI 0.83 to 0.94), which was increased by adding TIMP1 (AUC 0.92; 95% CI 0.88 to 0.96; p=0.06), LRG1 (AUC 0.92; 95% CI 0.88 to 0.96; p=0.02)
statements.note: CA19-9 alone gave AUC 0.88 in the testing set, and adding LRG1 gave AUC 0.92 (p=0.02).

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The combined marker panel separated early-stage PDAC from chronic pancreatitis as well as it separated PDAC from healthy controls.
statements.evidence: plasma markers were measured among PDAC cases and patients with chronic pancreatitis, colorectal cancer (CRC), and healthy controls.
statements.note: Chronic pancreatitis patients were sampled, but the abstract reports no discrimination result against them.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the validation set, a panel combining CA19-9, TIMP1 and nine-locus cfDNA methylation reached a higher AUC than CA19-9 alone.
statements.evidence: a combined panel including CA19-9, TIMP1 and a 9-loci cfDNA methylation panel had greater discrimination (AUC 0.86, 95% CI 0.77 to 0.95) than CA19-9 alone (AUC 0.82; 95% CI 0.72 to 0.92).
statements.note: In the 40-versus-40 validation set the combined panel reached AUC 0.86 against 0.82 for CA19-9 alone.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose plasma carried ESCC cfDNA methylation markers had shorter overall survival than patients without detectable markers.
statements.evidence: Our findings demonstrate the potential of multimodal analysis of cfDNA methylome for early detection and monitoring of molecular characteristics in ESCC.
statements.note: The abstract links methylation markers to molecular subtypes and tumor microenvironments, not to patient survival.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Integrating methylation, copy-number and fragmentation markers in the EMMA framework raised the AUC from 0.90 to 0.99.
statements.evidence: EMMA significantly improves detection rates, increasing AUCs from 0.90 to 0.99, and detects 87% of ESCCs and 62% of precancerous lesions with >95% specificity in validation cohorts.
statements.note: The abstract reports that EMMA lifted AUCs from 0.90 to 0.99.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among the three cfDNA marker types, methylation markers were more sensitive than copy-number or fragmentation features for detecting ESCC.
statements.evidence: cfDNA methylation markers are the earliest and most sensitive, detectable in 70% of ESCCs and 50% of precancerous lesions, and associated with molecular subtypes and tumor microenvironments.
statements.note: Methylation markers are described as the earliest and most sensitive of the three cfDNA marker types, found in 70% of ESCCs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the cfDNA sequencing data, copy-number and fragmentation features were highly specific, but they were associated with late-stage disease.
statements.evidence: CNVs and fragmentation features show high specificity but are linked to late-stage disease.
statements.note: The abstract describes CNV and fragmentation features as highly specific yet linked to late-stage disease.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A ctDNA genomic signature tracking retinoblastoma LOH was significantly associated with poor response to ET + CDK4/6i, independent of plasma tumor fraction.
statements.evidence: a ctDNA-based genomic signature tracking retinoblastoma loss-of-heterozygosity, are significantly associated with poor response and survival outcome following ET + CDK4/6i, independently of plasma tumor fraction.
statements.note: The retinoblastoma loss-of-heterozygosity signature is reported as significantly associated with poor response, independently of plasma tumor fraction.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Four DNA-based subtypes derived from plasma ctDNA were associated with poor response and shorter survival after ET + CDK4/6i treatment.
statements.evidence: More importantly, 4 DNA-based subtypes, and a ctDNA-based genomic signature tracking retinoblastoma loss-of-heterozygosity, are significantly associated with poor response and survival outcome following ET + CDK4/6i
statements.note: Four DNA-based subtypes were significantly associated with poor response and poor survival outcome following ET + CDK4/6i.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Machine-learning multi-gene signatures from ctDNA captured tumor proliferation and estrogen receptor signaling, much as direct tissue DNA or RNA profiling does.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that machine learning multi-gene signatures, obtained from ctDNA, identify complex biological features, including measures of tumor proliferation and estrogen receptor signaling, similar to what is accomplished using direct tumor tissue DNA or RNA profiling.
statements.note: The abstract states that ctDNA-derived signatures identified proliferation and estrogen receptor signaling, similar to direct tumor tissue profiling.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The ctDNA-derived DNA subtypes also predicted poor outcome in metastatic breast cancer patients treated with chemotherapy.
statements.evidence: To address this question, we have performed 0.5X shallow whole-genome sequencing in plasma from 459 patients with metastatic breast cancer, including 245 patients treated with endocrine therapy and a CDK4/6 inhibitor (ET + CDK4/6i) from 2 independent cohorts.
statements.note: Outcome associations are reported only for patients treated with ET + CDK4/6i; chemotherapy-treated patients are not analysed.

statements.label: not_addressed

statements.evidence: These findings indicate that the MCED test has strong potential to improve early cancer detection and support clinical decision-making.
statements.note: The abstract reports detection accuracy only; no mortality outcome was measured.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In the independent validation cohort, the MCED test predicted the cancer's tissue of origin with 82.4% accuracy.
statements.evidence: The results demonstrated an overall sensitivity of 87.4%, specificity of 97.8% and tissue-of-origin prediction accuracy of 82.4% in the independent validation cohort.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among 3,724 asymptomatic participants in a prospective study, the test reached a specificity of 98.1%.
statements.evidence: Preliminary results from a prospective study of 3,724 asymptomatic participants showed a sensitivity of 53.5% (predominantly early stage cancers) and specificity of 98.1%.
statements.note: The prospective study of asymptomatic participants reported 98.1% specificity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Sensitivity of the MCED test was lower in the prospective study of asymptomatic participants than in the independent validation cohort.
statements.evidence: sensitivity of 87.4%, specificity of 97.8% and tissue-of-origin prediction accuracy of 82.4% in the independent validation cohort. Preliminary results from a prospective study of 3,724 asymptomatic participants showed a sensitivity of 53.5%
statements.note: Sensitivity was 53.5% in the prospective asymptomatic study against 87.4% in the independent validation cohort.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Analysed separately in cfDNA with a tumor-informed approach, each of the three epigenomic features distinguished EGFRm LUAD from tSCLC with AUROCs of 0.82-0.87.
statements.evidence: Tumor-informed analysis of each of these three epigenomic features in cfDNA resulted in accurate noninvasive discrimination between patients with EGFRm LUAD versus tSCLC [area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) = 0.82-0.87].
statements.note: Each single epigenomic feature in cfDNA gave AUROCs between 0.82 and 0.87 for LUAD versus tSCLC.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The epigenomic cfDNA approach also detected small cell transformation in patients with ALK-rearranged lung adenocarcinoma.
statements.evidence: These data demonstrate the feasibility of detecting small cell transformation in patients with EGFRm LUAD through epigenomic cfDNA profiling of 1 mL of patient plasma.
statements.note: Only EGFR-mutant LUAD was studied; the abstract says nothing about other oncogene drivers such as ALK.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across the lung cancer xenografts, LUAD and tSCLC differed at more sites for H3K27ac than for DNA methylation.
statements.evidence: Analysis of 126 epigenomic libraries from the lung cancer PDXs revealed widespread epigenomic reprogramming between LUAD and tSCLC, with a large number of differential H3K27ac (n = 24,424), DNA methylation (n = 3,298), and chromatin accessibility (n = 16,352) sites between the two histologies.
statements.note: The xenograft analysis found 24,424 differential H3K27ac sites against 3,298 differential DNA methylation sites.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Combining the three epigenomic features into one cfDNA classifier yielded an AUROC of 0.94 for telling EGFRm LUAD apart from tSCLC.
statements.evidence: A multianalyte cfDNA-based classifier integrating these three epigenomic features discriminated between EGFRm LUAD versus tSCLC with an AUROC of 0.94.
statements.note: The integrated multianalyte cfDNA classifier reached an AUROC of 0.94.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Overall, driver rearrangements were detected at a lower prevalence in liquid biopsies than in tissue biopsies.
